Frank Ocean’s song **“Alabama”** is a brief, 1:24-minute track from his 2016 visual album *Endless*, named after **Alabama Street** in New Orleans’ Seabrook neighborhood where he spent formative years of his youth [1]. The song serves as a **reminiscent tale** of his childhood memories—family, friends, and his first love—capturing the relationships that defined that era of his life [1].

### SONG CREATION
- **Writing process & timeline**: The track was created as part of *Endless*, a visual album released on **August 19, 2016**, via Apple Music [1]. No specific interview details about the writing timeline are available in the provided premium sources.
- **Co-writers & collaborators**: Frank Ocean is credited as the **producer** of the song [1]. It features **additional vocals** from **Sampha** and **Jazmine Sullivan** [1].
- **Original inspiration**: Ocean explicitly stated the song is named after **Alabama Street**, where he grew up, and reflects on memories from that time [1]. In 2017, he shared a childhood photo captioned “Alabama St.” showing himself as “Lonny” Breaux with his mother, Katonya Breaux [1].
